model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.note: The agent definition's template text names claude-fable-5. That is template text, not the runtime identity. This evaluation was produced by the actual runtime model of the evaluating session, Opus 5 (1M context), exact model id claude-opus-5[1m], taken from the session environment. Both model.name and model.evaluator_model carry that runtime identity.

issues_detected.description: content_warnings[0].content_warnings_present is false, yet the same entry populates a warnings list carrying the healthsheet's free-speech offensive-language warning. The prose explains that the warning describes an earlier release and that version 3.1.0 does not distribute the free speech content it concerns, so the reasoning is sound, but a false boolean paired with a populated warnings array is contradictory in shape and a machine reader consuming either field alone gets the opposite answer.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep content_warnings_present false and move the superseded healthsheet warning into source_caveats or notes, so the warnings list is empty when the boolean is false.

issues_detected.description: confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present is false, sourced to the healthsheet's 'No' answer, while regulatory_restrictions sets confidentiality_level to restricted, records a Certificate of Confidentiality that must be asserted against subpoenas, and quotes the Data Transfer and Use Agreement describing the data as personally identifiable information under OMB Memorandum M-07-16. sensitive_elements_present is simultaneously true for race, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health content. The record's own source_caveats scopes the false answer to the feature-only release, which is a defensible reading, but the three governance slots still signal opposite confidentiality postures.
issues_detected.recommendation: State in confidential_elements that the doctor-patient-privilege reading of the healthsheet question is what is being answered, and cross-reference the Certificate of Confidentiality and the restricted classification so the three slots read as one position.

issues_detected.description: involves_human_subjects is true with a documented residual re-identification risk ('a person's voice is unique to them and to their health at that time, so it is always possible, even if unlikely, that someone could recognize a participant by voice') and an explicit statement that k-anonymization with k of at least two was not achieved, but no data_protection_impacts slot is present anywhere in the record. regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact is likewise absent while the Data Access Compliance Office address DACO@b2ai-voice.org is recorded under maintainers.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add data_protection_impacts recording the impact analysis behind the decision to withhold waveforms, or state that none was conducted, and lift the DACO address into regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact rather than leaving it only in maintainers.

issues_detected.description: sensitive_elements inventories race, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, socioeconomic and health information as present, while its own source_caveats records that all fields encoded as sensitive in the REDCap data dictionary were removed at version 3.0.0 together with household income, mental health status and traumatic life experiences. The record names the contradiction and reports both sides rather than resolving it, so the reader cannot tell which sensitive attributes the released tables actually carry.
issues_detected.recommendation: Enumerate which demographic attributes survive in the released phenotype tables, distinguishing them from those removed at the 3.0.0 de-identification stage.

issues_detected.description: cleaning_strategies describes an audit protocol of missingness tables, distribution and outlier checks, schema validation of categorical responses and audio quality control, while its source_caveats records the healthsheet answering 'No' to whether any preprocessing for cleaning was done. The record attributes the audit steps to release-time quality control drawn from other documentation, which is a reasonable reconciliation, but the two statements are left side by side.
issues_detected.recommendation: State that the healthsheet 'No' refers to value-level cleaning and that the audit protocol is release-time quality control, so the two are not in conflict.

issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes records that data were collected over twelve months, while the same entry's caveat traces cohort accrual from 306 participants at version 1.0 to 833 at version 3.0.0 across releases dated January 2025 to May 2026, and distribution_dates lists five releases spanning sixteen months. The twelve-month figure is flagged as possibly not describing the released cohort, but it remains the only value in the slot and no start or end date is given.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record a dated collection window per version, or scope the twelve-month statement explicitly to the initial release cohort.

issues_detected.description: version_access.latest_version_doi carries doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42, which the record itself identifies in related_datasets as the concept DOI resolving to the latest version, not the DOI of the latest version. The DOI of the latest version is 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, this record's own doi. The slot name and the value therefore disagree, although version_details explains the concept-DOI arrangement and the is_version_of relation types it correctly.
issues_detected.recommendation: Put the version DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 in latest_version_doi and keep the concept DOI in version_details and the is_version_of relation.

issues_detected.description: Identifier form is inconsistent within related_datasets.target_dataset: three entries carry bare DOI strings (10.13026/h995-bt35, 10.13026/k81f-qr68, 10.13026/37yb-1t42) with no doi: prefix, while version_access.latest_version_doi in the same record does use the doi: CURIE form, and a fourth entry carries a bare Synapse accession, syn72370534, with no prefix or resolvable form at all. The top-level id is a physionet.org content URL rather than a resolver URL, so it is not a case the v8 write-time resolver-URL normalisation covers.
issues_detected.recommendation: Use one identifier form across target_dataset, either doi: CURIEs throughout or bare DOIs throughout, and express the Synapse accession as a resolvable identifier.

issues_detected.description: notes reports the project's AI-readiness self-assessment as 'Sustainability 50 percent with the domain-appropriate and associated criteria not met', while the record elsewhere documents hosting on PhysioNet, a domain-appropriate biomedical repository, with per-version and concept DOIs, a named maintaining institution and its NIBIB, NHLBI and NIH Office of the Director grant support. source_caveats records that several documentation answers were written against Health Data Nexus hosting; the self-assessment appears to be one of them, but it is carried into notes without that scoping.
issues_detected.recommendation: Scope the quoted sustainability self-assessment to the release and hosting platform it was written against, as the record already does for the healthsheet and study metadata answers.

issues_detected.description: variables enumerates only four elements, all of them join keys and recording metadata (participant_id, session_id, task_name, n_frames), while the record describes a phenotype directory of demographic, confounder, per-condition diagnosis, enrollment, questionnaire and task tables and eleven feature files, each with a JSON data dictionary. The variables slot therefore describes the linkage layer rather than the dataset's variables, which is coherent with the record's own account of the data dictionaries carrying the column-level semantics, but it under-populates the slot the schema names for that purpose.
issues_detected.recommendation: Either extend variables to the principal phenotype and feature columns, or note in the slot that column-level semantics are delegated to the distributed JSON data dictionaries.

issues_detected.description: keywords carries four generic terms (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice) while the description enumerates modality, five cohort categories, eight feature families, three distribution formats and the credentialed access model. Discoverability is materially below what the record itself documents.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add terms for modality (speech, cough, acoustic features), cohort (voice disorders, neurological, psychiatric, respiratory), format (Parquet, TSV) and access model (credentialed access).

semantic_insights: DOI prefixes are all plausible and correctly attributed: 10.13026 is PhysioNet's registrant prefix, used for this release (8xbn-nq66), the concept DOI (37yb-1t42), the preceding version 3.0.0 (k81f-qr68) and the companion pediatric dataset (h995-bt35).
RRID:SCR_007345 in the citation matches the RRID:SCR_ pattern and is PhysioNet's registered resource identifier, so its placement inside a PhysioNet dataset citation is semantically correct.

Grant identifiers follow NIH form: OT2OD032720 parses as activity code OT2, institute OD, serial 032720, and 3OT2OD032720-01S1 as a type-3 supplement of that core project. The record documents four divergent surface forms across sources, including two garbled ones in the project documentation, and states which source is preferred and why.

The five-condition applicability resolution is unambiguous: human participants are evidenced from description and collection_mechanisms; sharing from distribution_formats with PhysioNet access URLs and a license permitting general research use; software output from GitHub repositories in external_resources; collection from acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, data_collectors and collection_timeframes; publication from a formal dataset citation. All twenty questions are applicable and none is excluded from the denominator.

The de-identification method is appropriate to the data type. Voice is a biometric, and the release answers that by withholding the waveform entirely and distributing derived features, layering HIPAA Safe Harbor removal, indirect-identifier removal, transcript review for external voices and withholding of dense features for sensitive and free-speech records on top. The failure to reach k-anonymity of two is stated rather than concealed.

The two-tier access model is internally coherent end to end: credentialed PhysioNet access with a signed Registered Access Agreement for the feature release, and a separate DACO-reviewed Data Transfer and Use Agreement route via Synapse for the raw audio, with ip_restrictions, prohibited_uses, retention_limit and third_party_sharing all drawn from the same instruments.

Temporal ordering is consistent throughout: award period 2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30, five dated releases from 2025-01-17 to 2026-05-01, issued and last_updated_on both 2026-05-01 matching the version 3.1.0 release date in distribution_dates and version_access.

Provenance is recoverable as a chain rather than a version list: was_derived_from names the REDCap exports and tablet-captured audio, raw_sources gives the controlled-access Synapse location, preprocessing_strategies gives the signal-processing parameters (25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, 60 MFCCs, 50 Hz articulatory rate, 100 Hz posteriorgrams), machine_annotation_tools names the eight tools and b2aiprep version 3.0.0, and file_collections enumerates the resulting artifacts.

The companion pediatric dataset is kept out of this record's composition and expressed as a typed is_supplemented_by relation with its own DOI, its own REB approval and its own Synapse raw-audio location, and subpopulations states that the pediatric category is released separately. That matches the project's declared scope separation.

known_biases uses four BiasTypeEnum values (selection_bias, representation_bias, measurement_bias, annotation_bias) with mitigation_strategy on two and affected_subsets on one, and future_use_impacts carries the downstream consequence that models may learn site or device signatures rather than disease signatures.

Per-feature record counts (29,278 spectrogram, 32,522 torchaudio pitch, 28,640 articulatory, 31,855 loudness, 31,872 periodicity, 29,289 posteriorgram) are stated with the reason they cannot be summed, and source_caveats separately records that no total recording count is given for 3.1.0. The arithmetic is not asserted where the sources do not support it.

correctness_validations.doi_format: valid (10.13026 PhysioNet x4: 8xbn-nq66 release, 37yb-1t42 concept, k81f-qr68 v3.0.0, h995-bt35 pediatric); one slot-semantics mismatch, latest_version_doi carries the concept DOI
correctness_validations.grant_number_format: valid (OT2OD032720 core; 3OT2OD032720-01S1 supplement; divergent source forms declared in funders.source_caveats)
correctness_validations.url_validity: all plausible (physionet.org, b2ai-voice.org, docs.b2ai-voice.org, synapse.org, four github.com repositories); one non-URL, non-CURIE identifier in related_datasets.target_dataset (bare Synapse accession syn72370534)

questions.name: Field Completeness
questions.description: Proportion of mandatory schema fields populated
questions.evidence: Present (12/14): id 'https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/'; title 'Bridge2AI-Voice: An ethically-sourced, diverse voice dataset linked to health information'; description (~1,900 chars); keywords (4); license_and_use_terms (data_use_permission general_research_use plus detailed license_terms); doi '10.13026/8xbn-nq66'; page 'https://b2ai-voice.org/'; creators (3 entries, two with named principal investigators and affiliations, one with 12 consortium affiliations); purposes (3); instances (3 instance types, 833 participants plus per-feature record counts); variables (4); regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level 'restricted'. Absent (2/14): resources; parent_datasets.
questions.quality_note: 12 of 14 named fields populated with substantive content (85.7%), between the 70% and 90% anchors. Both absences are partially compensated elsewhere: the file inventory sits in file_collections and distribution_formats, and version lineage is expressed as typed related_datasets relations (is_new_version_of, is_version_of, derives_from). variables is populated but thin at four join-key entries against a record describing dozens of phenotype and feature tables.

questions.name: Entry Length Adequacy
questions.description: Whether narrative fields have meaningful content length
questions.evidence: description: ~1,900 chars naming 833 participants, five North American sites, the four adult cohort categories, the derived-feature inventory ('spectrograms, Mel spectrograms, Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, articulatory and source measures from Speech Articulatory Coding, phonetic posteriorgrams, pitch contours'), the phenotype directory contents, the collection instrument, the distribution formats and the credentialed access model. purposes: three entries of roughly 180 to 280 chars, supplemented by addressing_gaps (4 entries) and tasks (2 entries).
questions.quality_note: Far above the 200-character anchor and non-boilerplate throughout. The description does real work: it states what the release excludes (the waveforms) as prominently as what it includes, which is the single most consequential fact for a reuser.

questions.name: Keyword Diversity
questions.description: Number of unique keywords
questions.evidence: keywords: 'health', 'biomarkers', 'bridge2ai', 'voice' (4 unique).
questions.quality_note: Middle band only. None of the four terms captures modality (speech, cough, acoustic features), cohort (voice, neurological, psychiatric, respiratory disorders), format (Parquet, TSV) or access model, all of which the record documents in detail elsewhere. Discoverability is the weakest structural dimension of an otherwise dense record.

questions.name: File Enumeration and Type Variety
questions.description: Number of distribution formats and file type diversity
questions.evidence: distribution_formats: two entries, 'Parquet' and 'Tab-separated values with JSON data dictionaries', each with a PhysioNet access URL and notes. file_collections enumerates three collections and names eleven feature files individually (ppgs.parquet, sparc_ema.parquet, sparc_loudness.parquet, sparc_periodicity.parquet, sparc_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_spectrogram.parquet, torchaudio_mfcc.parquet, torchaudio_pitch.parquet, torchaudio_mel_spectrogram.parquet, static_features.tsv, audio_quality_metrics.tsv), a metadata Parquet file, and a phenotype directory of tab-delimited tables across five subdirectories. Three distinct types: Parquet, TSV, JSON. total_file_count absent; no format is named for the controlled-access raw audio.
questions.quality_note: Three formats, at the top of the 2-3 band, with per-file enumeration and a stated pairing rule (every table has a JSON data dictionary sharing its file stem) that is more useful than a bare format count. Short of the >3 anchor because the raw audio format is never named and no file count or size is given.

questions.name: Data File Size Availability
questions.description: Presence of file size or instance count metadata
questions.evidence: instances[0].counts: 833 participants. instances[1].notes gives per-feature record counts: 29,278 spectrogram, Mel spectrogram and MFCC records; 32,522 torchaudio pitch; 28,640 articulatory; 31,855 loudness; 31,872 periodicity and Speech Articulatory Coding pitch; 29,289 phonetic posteriorgram. splits records that no recommended splits are supplied and users should create their own. subpopulations describes two subpopulation dimensions. total_size_bytes and file_collections.total_bytes are absent.
questions.quality_note: Passes on instance counts at two granularities, participant and per-feature record. No byte figure anywhere, so size can only be estimated, and the record states that the per-feature counts cannot be summed to a recording total because they count overlapping recordings.

questions.name: Dataset Identification Metadata
questions.description: Presence of unique identifiers such as DOI, RRID, or persistent URLs
questions.evidence: doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66 (PhysioNet registrant prefix). id: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/. page: https://b2ai-voice.org/. publisher: https://physionet.org/. version_access.latest_version_doi: doi:10.13026/37yb-1t42 (concept DOI). citation carries RRID:SCR_007345. related_datasets carries three further DOIs and a Synapse accession.
questions.quality_note: Multiple persistent identifiers at both version and concept granularity, plus an RRID, all with plausible registrar prefixes. Comfortable pass.

questions.name: Funding and Acknowledgements Completeness
questions.description: Presence of funding sources, grants, creator affiliations, and institutional sponsors
questions.score_label: Funders with grants + creators with affiliations
questions.evidence: funders: grantor 'National Institutes of Health Common Fund, Bridge2AI Program' with two grants, 3OT2OD032720-01S1 (PhysioNet acknowledgements, with the funded project title quoted) and OT2OD032720 (NIH RePORTER core project number and the organization study identifier), each with its own provenance note; source_caveats reconciles five divergent surface forms across sources and records the RePORTER award amount (4,660,942) and project period (2022-09-01 to 2026-11-30). creators: University of South Florida with principal investigator Yael Bensoussan and affiliation, Weill Cornell Medicine with principal investigator Olivier Elemento and affiliation, and the Bridge2AI-Voice Consortium with twelve named member institutions. maintainers additionally records PhysioNet's own support under U24EB037545 and R01EB030362.
questions.quality_note: The strongest funding block available: named grantor, multiple award identifiers with per-identifier provenance, an explicit preference rule for which form governs, creator affiliations at both institution and individual level, and the hosting platform's separate grant support. The garbled documentation forms are recorded rather than silently corrected, which is the right handling.

questions.name: Ethical and Privacy Declarations
questions.applicability_evidence: Human-subjects condition is met from fields outside Q8: description states 'Version 3.1.0 contains data for 833 adult participants recruited across five sites in North America'; keywords include 'health'; collection_mechanisms describes a tablet application that 'administers demographic surveys, confounder questions and validated questionnaires' to participants in clinic. Applicability is therefore established without reference to any Q8 field.
questions.description: Comprehensive ethics coverage including IRB, deidentification, privacy, consent, compensation and vulnerable populations
questions.score_label: Near-comprehensive; data protection impact assessment absent
questions.evidence: ethical_reviews: USF Institutional Review Board, with United States sites joining through the Single IRB process and subsite approvals under it. human_subject_research: involves_human_subjects true, ethics_review_board named, irb_approval text, regulatory_compliance (HIPAA, Certificate of Confidentiality, Single IRB), special_populations (neurological and neurodegenerative diagnoses including Alzheimer's, ALS and Parkinson's; mood and psychiatric diagnoses including depression, bipolar, anxiety, PTSD, ADHD). informed_consent: consent_obtained true, four consent modes including a video-read statement that doubles as voice-identity verification, consent_documentation with a five-year retention rule, consent_scope covering registered and controlled tiers and EHR access for gold-standard validation, withdrawal_mechanism stating data cannot be removed once collection completes. collection_consents, collection_notifications and consent_revocations each populated. is_deidentified: identifiable_elements_present false, method 'HIPAA Safe Harbor de-identification, supplemented by removal of indirect identifiers...', a nineteen-item identifiers_removed list, and deidentification_details conceding 'k-anonymization with k of at least two was not achieved'. participant_privacy: anonymization_method, privacy_techniques (HIPAA firewall, trained personnel, HTTPS, NIH STRIDES storage), reidentification_risk, data_linkage. participant_compensation: gift cards, 40 USD under 90 minutes, 80 USD over, capped at three sessions and 120 USD total. regulatory_restrictions.hipaa_compliant 'compliant' with other_compliance recording the Certificate of Confidentiality and OMB M-07-16 status. Absent: data_protection_impacts; at_risk_populations as a slot; regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact.
questions.quality_note: Ethics coverage is close to complete and unusually candid: the residual voice re-identification risk and the failure to reach k-anonymity of two are stated rather than smoothed over, and the classification values for confidentiality_level and hipaa_compliant carry a caveat saying neither term is used verbatim by any source. Held to 4 by the absence of data_protection_impacts, which the rubric names explicitly in the 5 anchor and which matters here given the documented residual risk, and by the DACO governance contact living in maintainers rather than in the governance slot. The confidential_elements false / sensitive_elements true / restricted-classification tension noted in semantic_analysis also weighs against a 5.

questions.name: Access Requirements and Governance Documentation
questions.description: Whether access policy, license, IP restrictions, regulatory restrictions and confidentiality level are clearly defined
questions.evidence: license: 'Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access License'. license_and_use_terms: data_use_permission general_research_use; license_terms giving the credentialed policy for 3.1.0 (credentialed PhysioNet users signing the Registered Access Agreement, no additional training), the separate controlled-access route for raw audio (Data Access Request Form, DUA, DACO review, institution-signed DTUA), the consent's explicit non-restriction on commercial use, geography, research type or algorithm development, and the requirement that collaborators apply independently; source_caveats records the access model changing from restricted (v1.1) to credentialed (v3.0.0, v3.1.0). ip_restrictions: five clauses covering copyright non-transfer, permitted duplication and prohibited sale, no IP claims on the data, downstream IP subject to non-obstructive licensing and the Fort Lauderdale Agreement, and absence of third-party IP restrictions. regulatory_restrictions: confidentiality_level 'restricted', hipaa_compliant 'compliant', a restrictions list (no export controls; credentialed access; institutional sign-off for raw audio), other_compliance (Certificate of Confidentiality, OMB M-07-16 PII status, PhysioNet obligations), and a source_caveats stating the basis for both classification values. retention_limit gives indefinite hosting against a two-year recipient destruction obligation with a thirty-day certification requirement.
questions.quality_note: Full marks. License, restrictions and confidentiality classification are all present, the two access tiers are documented end to end from application through destruction, and the classification values are explicitly labelled as the record's own reading of the sources rather than quoted terms. The only gap against the named field list is data_protection_impacts, which does not affect this anchor.

questions.name: Interoperability, Standardization, and Cross-Platform Integration
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition is met: distribution_formats is populated with two format entries each carrying access_urls to https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/, and license_and_use_terms sets data_use_permission to general_research_use under a credentialed access policy that permits both commercial and non-commercial research.
questions.description: Standard formats, ontology and schema conformance, cross-platform linkage and integration capability
questions.score_label: Standard formats + partial semantic annotation + integration capability
questions.evidence: distribution_formats: Parquet ('an open-source column-oriented data file format... can be loaded with any library that supports Parquet') and tab-delimited text with companion JSON data dictionaries 'whose keys match the column names of the table'. Ontology annotation on instances: data_topic B2AI_TOPIC:36, B2AI_TOPIC:37, B2AI_TOPIC:31 and data_substrate B2AI_SUBSTRATE:30, B2AI_SUBSTRATE:80 as CURIEs. conforms_to_schema: https://w3id.org/bridge2ai/data-sheets-schema with conforms_to_class Dataset. related_datasets: four typed relations (is_supplemented_by, is_new_version_of, is_version_of, derives_from) each with a target identifier. external_resources: six entries with URLs including four GitHub repositories with their licenses (Apache-2.0, MIT). Integration keys documented in variables: participant_id 'present in every feature and phenotype table', session_id, task_name, and relationships explains how feature, metadata and phenotype tables join. conforms_to and conforms_to_standard are deliberately omitted, with source_caveats explaining that the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion described in the documentation concerns the audio dataset's folder layout rather than this feature-only release. file_collections.compression not stated.
questions.quality_note: Standard, non-proprietary formats throughout, machine-readable column semantics via per-table JSON dictionaries, B2AI ontology CURIEs on every instance type, typed cross-dataset relations with resolvable identifiers, and an explicitly documented join key present in every table. Short of 5 because the data themselves declare conformance to no domain standard: the record correctly declines to claim BIDS conformance it cannot support, which is honest, but it leaves the dataset with no data-level schema or standard reference, and no compression or checksum metadata.

questions.name: Tool and Software Transparency
questions.applicability_evidence: Software-tools condition is met from a field outside Q11: external_resources (a Q14 field) names four code repositories as dataset outputs, including 'b2aiprep, the library used to organize and preprocess the dataset and to merge the source data into the phenotype files, released under Apache-2.0: https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep' and 'senselab... https://github.com/sensein/senselab'. extension_mechanism.contribution_url points at the same b2aiprep repository. Applicability is therefore established without reference to any Q11 field.
questions.description: Preprocessing, cleaning and labeling strategies with the software tools used
questions.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: two entries giving standardization (monaural conversion, 16 kHz resampling, Butterworth anti-aliasing filter) and feature extraction with exact parameters (25 ms window, 10 ms hop, 400-point FFT, downsampled by two in time giving 201 frequency bins; sixty MFCCs and a sixty-bin Mel spectrogram; six articulators as electromagnetic articulography estimates with loudness, periodicity and pitch at 50 Hz; forty phoneme categories at 100 Hz), naming b2aiprep 'version 3.0.0 for this release' and senselab. cleaning_strategies: a four-step audit protocol plus audio quality control on silence, duration and passage fidelity, with a source_caveats recording the healthsheet's contrary 'No'. labeling_strategies: clinical assessment protocol, cohort-specific gold-standard methods (laryngoscopy and stroboscopy, spirometry and flow volume loops, brain CT and MRI, psychiatric EHR and medication history), annotations_per_item 1, annotator_demographics, data_annotation_protocol (Bridge2AI protocols and ICD-10) and data_annotation_platform (REDCap). machine_annotation_tools: eight tools listed (OpenAI Whisper Large, openSMILE, Praat via parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc, ppgs, b2aiprep, senselab) with a per-tool description of what each produced and a tool_accuracy caveat that off-the-shelf models were not audited for correctness. missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling_strategy stating values are left missing rather than imputed and a missingness table is distributed. imputation_protocols and annotation_analyses absent.
questions.quality_note: Very good, with a genuine gap. Strategies are comprehensive and the signal-processing parameters are specific enough to reproduce the feature extraction, and repository URLs are supplied for the two consortium libraries. Held to 4 because only b2aiprep carries a version: openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc, ppgs and senselab are named without versions, and 'Whisper Large' identifies a model size rather than a release, so the pipeline is described but not pinned. imputation_protocols is absent, though handling_strategy answers the question by stating no imputation was performed.

questions.name: Collection Protocol Clarity
questions.applicability_evidence: Both halves of the condition hold. Collection fields are populated: acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, data_collectors and collection_timeframes all carry entries. Datasets shared is established from distribution_formats with PhysioNet access URLs and a license permitting general research use.
questions.description: Completeness of collection mechanisms, acquisition methods, collectors and timeframes
questions.evidence: acquisition_methods: all four booleans set (directly observed, reported by subjects, inferred/derived, validated/verified) with acquisition_details distinguishing observed acoustics, self-reported demographics and questionnaires, clinician-verified diagnoses, and released values that are 'inferred or derived rather than observed directly'. collection_mechanisms: the Bridge2AI-Voice tablet application with device models (iPad 9th or 10th generation, iPad Air 5th generation), microphone (Avid AE-36 through an Apple dongle), headset use and task inventory; and REDCap for clinical, diagnostic and questionnaire capture with an open-source export library. data_collectors: site research teams (recruitment, consent, supervised collection, including students coordinating with clinicians) and site clinicians (diagnosis and gold-standard validation, listed as IRB co-investigators). direct_collection: is_direct true, collected in clinic in the United States and Canada. sampling_strategies: non-probability, is_random false, is_representative false, recruitment from high-volume expert clinics against cohort-specific inclusion and exclusion criteria screened before the visit, with controls, and a why_not_representative statement. raw_sources: origin of the waveforms and REDCap data with a controlled-access Synapse URL. collection_timeframes: 'the data were collected over a period of twelve months. No collection start or end dates are given for this release', with a caveat that the figure may not describe the released cohort's accrual.
questions.quality_note: Methods, mechanisms, collectors and instruments are documented to an unusual level of specificity, down to tablet generation and microphone model, which is exactly what a reuser needs to reason about device confounding. Held to 4 by the timeframes dimension alone: the slot is populated but carries no dates, and the record itself flags that the twelve-month figure may not describe the span over which the 833-participant cohort was assembled.

questions.name: Version History, Maintenance, and Sustainability
questions.applicability_evidence: Same condition as Q12: collection fields are populated (acquisition_methods, collection_mechanisms, data_collectors, collection_timeframes) and the dataset is shared through PhysioNet under a license permitting general research use.
questions.description: Version information, access, errata, update plans, and data sustainability
questions.evidence: version: 3.1.0. version_access: six versions enumerated with dates and per-version deltas (1.0 on Health Data Nexus with 12,523 recordings from 306 participants; 1.1 adding MFCCs; 2.0.0 adding 136 participants and reprocessing spectrograms; 2.0.1 authorship corrections; 3.0.0 adding 391 participants and splitting the phenotype file; 3.1.0 adding data for existing participants, fixing Parquet files and adding quality metrics), a concept DOI, and version_details on per-version DOIs, continued hosting of older versions, the unavailability of 1.1 files and the publisher's reserved right to withdraw older versions. errata: three entries covering the 3.1.0, 2.0 and 2.0.1 corrections, with a caveat that the documentation claims no erratum exists and these are drawn from PhysioNet release notes. updates: semi-annual frequency, new versions rather than in-place edits each with its own DOI, notification through platform news items, with a caveat that the cadence was stated against Health Data Nexus hosting. maintainers: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology, which maintains PhysioNet under NIBIB, NHLBI and NIH Office of the Director grants U24EB037545 and R01EB030362, and the consortium's Data Access Compliance Office. publisher: PhysioNet, a domain-appropriate biomedical repository. retention_limit and extension_mechanism give the preservation and contribution routes.
questions.quality_note: All four sustainability signals the rubric names are present: persistent identifiers at version and concept level, a governance plan spanning retention and access review, a domain-appropriate repository, and documented institutional commitment through the hosting platform's own named grant support. The version history is exhaustive and each version's delta is stated. One inconsistency, noted in semantic_analysis, is that the record's quoted AI-readiness self-assessment scores sustainability at 50 percent with the domain-appropriate criterion unmet, which the record's own evidence contradicts.

questions.name: Associated Publications
questions.applicability_evidence: Publication condition is met: citation carries a full formal dataset citation ('Bensoussan, Y., Sigaras, A., Rameau, A., ... Ghosh, S. (2026). Bridge2AI-Voice... (version 3.1.0). PhysioNet. RRID:SCR_007345. https://doi.org/10.13026/8xbn-nq66') and external_resources lists six referenced resources. Datasets shared is established from distribution_formats and the license.
questions.description: Formal citations or external resources with DOI-linked references
questions.score_label: Formal dataset citation plus multiple resources; no publication DOIs
questions.evidence: citation: complete dataset citation with twenty named authors and an et-al elision, version, publisher, RRID and resolvable DOI link. external_resources: six entries, each with a URL, covering the project documentation site (protocols, healthsheet, study metadata, AI-readiness assessment), b2aiprep, senselab, the Bridge2AI REDCap data dictionary repository, the documentation site source, and the controlled-access raw audio on Synapse, with future_guarantees and access restrictions stated. related_datasets: four typed relations, three carrying DOIs. Absent: no journal or preprint citation. source_caveats refers to 'the feasibility publication' and 'the audiomics white paper' as consulted sources and quotes a grant number from the former, but neither is cited with a title, author, venue or DOI.
questions.quality_note: Strong on dataset citation and supporting resources: a formal, resolvable citation and six referenced resources with licenses and access conditions. Held to 4 because the two scholarly publications the record demonstrably relied on are named only descriptively in source_caveats and are not citable from this record, so a reader cannot follow the record's own evidence trail to them.

questions.name: Human Subject Representation
questions.applicability_evidence: Same human-subjects condition as Q8, established from fields outside Q15: description ('833 adult participants recruited across five sites in North America'), keywords ('health'), and collection_mechanisms (a tablet application administering demographic surveys and validated questionnaires to participants in clinic).
questions.description: Inclusion of human subjects, demographic diversity and subgroup detail
questions.score_label: Subgroups characterized; no distributions or counts
questions.evidence: instances: 833 participants with label true, a label_description explaining how diagnostic labels were established per cohort, three missing_information entries with reasons, and a note that a participant may appear on more than one row. subpopulations: two entries, the first naming the recorded dimensions ('Age, gender, sex, ethnicity and socioeconomic status are recorded, together with race and sexual orientation') with a distribution statement that the dataset 'has skews based on disorder category, site and other demographic factors'; the second naming the five disease cohort categories and stating this adult release covers four plus controls, that the pediatric category is a separate dataset, and that releases 'do not contain an equal distribution of the disease categories'. sampling_strategies: screening against cohort-specific inclusion and exclusion criteria, with controls enrolled. known_limitations: fluent English speakers only, with non-English speakers excluded, and a non-probability sample from five expert clinics. human_subject_research.special_populations names the neurological and psychiatric cohorts. missing_data_documentation records systematic absence of disease-specific fields outside a participant's cohort. Absent: at_risk_populations as a slot; any numeric demographic distribution, per-cohort count or subsets/splits breakdown.
questions.quality_note: Well above general human data: the recorded demographic dimensions are enumerated, the cohort structure is characterized, exclusions are stated with reasons, and the skew is acknowledged. Held to 4 because not one demographic figure appears anywhere. The record states the dataset has skews by disorder, site and demographics but gives no per-cohort, per-site, sex, age or race counts, so a reuser cannot assess representativeness quantitatively, and the specific cohort inclusion and exclusion criteria are referred to rather than listed.

questions.name: Findability (Persistent Links)
questions.description: Persistent URLs for access and documentation
questions.evidence: page: https://b2ai-voice.org/. id: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/. doi: 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, with the resolver form in the citation. distribution_formats access_urls: https://physionet.org/content/b2ai-voice/3.1.0/ on both entries. external_resources: https://docs.b2ai-voice.org/, four github.com repositories, https://www.synapse.org/Synapse:syn72370534/. extension_mechanism.contribution_url: https://github.com/sensein/b2aiprep. raw_sources.access_url: the Synapse location.
questions.quality_note: Numerous persistent and plausible links across the landing page, the repository, the documentation site, the code and the controlled-access raw audio. Comfortable pass.

questions.name: Accessibility (Access Mechanism)
questions.applicability_evidence: Datasets-shared condition is met: distribution_formats carries PhysioNet access URLs, third_party_sharing sets is_shared true and describes distribution 'to individuals outside the entity that created it, through PhysioNet, under credentialed access with a signed data use agreement', and the license permits general research use.
questions.description: How users obtain the dataset (download, DUA, login)
questions.score_label: Fully defined access path (platform, login, policy)
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms.license_terms: 'the access policy is credentialed: only credentialed users who sign the Bridge2AI Voice Registered Access Agreement may access the files, and no additional training is required', with the separate controlled-access route for raw audio requiring a Data Access Request Form, a Data Use Agreement, DACO review and an institution-signed Data Transfer and Use Agreement, and the requirement that collaborators and other teams at the same organization apply independently. distribution_formats: both entries carry the PhysioNet access URL and describe how the files load. third_party_sharing: the two-tier sharing model. maintainers: the DACO 'receives questions about access at DACO@b2ai-voice.org'. raw_sources.access_url and external_resources give the Synapse location for the controlled tier. source_caveats records that the access model changed from restricted at v1.1 to credentialed at v3.0.0 and v3.1.0, and which statement governs.
questions.quality_note: Full marks. Platform, credentialing requirement, agreement to be signed, training requirement (none), the distinct route and paperwork for the raw audio, the reviewing body, its contact address and the per-institution scope of an approval are all stated. A prospective user can determine exactly what they must do for either tier. The download_url slot is unpopulated but access_urls carry the equivalent information.

questions.name: Reusability, Use Guidance, and Social Impact
questions.description: License with explicit use guidance and social impact analysis with mitigations
questions.score_label: License + comprehensive use guidance + social impact analysis with mitigation
questions.evidence: license_and_use_terms as above, including the consent's explicit non-restriction on commercial use, geography, research type, genetic research and algorithm development. intended_uses: three categories (clinical machine-learning research, AI model pretraining and fine-tuning, voice biomarker research) each with examples and two with usage_notes, one stating the dataset 'is intended strictly for research that prioritizes patient safety, privacy and ethical use'. prohibited_uses: four, covering re-identification attempts, foreseeable harm or stigmatization to participants, families, communities or populations, IP-based restriction of access to the data or conclusions, and contacting subjects without IRB approval, provider approval and consent. discouraged_uses: two, naming hiring decisions, insurance premium adjustment and surveillance that could lead to discrimination or harm, and uses that assume representativeness. future_use_impacts: two entries, the first warning that skews by disorder, site and demographics risk 'unfair treatment of individuals or groups through stereotyping or quality-of-service failures', the second that models may learn site or device signatures rather than disease signatures. existing_uses records prior use in the Bridge2AI Summer School and hackathon and links training opportunities. known_biases carries mitigation_strategy entries.
questions.quality_note: Full marks. All five named fields are populated, the prohibited and discouraged categories are distinct and specific rather than boilerplate, and the impact analysis is framed in recognizable responsible-AI harm terms (stereotyping, quality-of-service failure, discriminatory surveillance) with mitigations offered both as user guidance (consider the multivariate distribution) and as project commitments (remote collection, Spanish protocols, recruitment designed to control more variables).

questions.name: Data Integrity, Provenance Graph, and Quality
questions.description: Version access, errata, updates, derivation, parent datasets, missing data, splits and provenance representation
questions.score_label: Recoverable lineage with typed derivation; not a full provenance graph
questions.evidence: version_access, errata (three entries) and updates all populated as under Q13. was_derived_from: 'Raw voice, speech and respiratory audio recordings and questionnaire responses collected under the Bridge2AI Voice Data Acquisition protocol and exported from REDCap' (prose, not a typed identifier). raw_sources: the origin waveforms and REDCap capture, with the controlled-access Synapse URL and a note that the BIDS 1.9.0 conversion describes the audio dataset rather than this release. related_datasets: a typed derives_from relation to the raw audio (syn72370534) and a typed is_new_version_of relation to version 3.0.0 (10.13026/k81f-qr68). missing_data_documentation: patterns, causes and handling strategy, with a distributed missingness table. anomalies: four entries covering configuration drift across sites, noise sources, unaudited off-the-shelf models and recordings that could not yield features. cleaning_strategies: the release audit protocol and the new audio quality metrics table. splits: no recommended splits, users create their own. Absent: parent_datasets; subsets.is_data_split; no PROV-O or entity-activity-agent structure.
questions.quality_note: Lineage is genuinely recoverable end to end, and the agents in it are named: participants and tablet application capture the audio, REDCap captures the clinical data, site clinicians assign labels, b2aiprep 3.0.0 and senselab with the eight named tools compute features at stated parameters, and the outputs are enumerated per file. Derivation is typed once, through related_datasets.derives_from. Held to 4 because parent_datasets is empty, was_derived_from is prose rather than an identifier, no entity-activity-agent structure or per-variable derivation is expressed, and no checksums or file-level integrity metadata are given, so the graph must be reconstructed by a reader from narrative across seven slots.

questions.name: Bias Documentation and Responsible AI Alignment
questions.applicability_evidence: Not gated by the sharing condition: a dataset that is never released still has documentable biases.
questions.description: Known biases using standard taxonomies with fairness analysis
questions.score_label: Taxonomy-categorized biases with mitigations; no fairness quantification
questions.evidence: known_biases: four entries typed with BiasTypeEnum values. selection_bias, that groups with less trust in the medical system or in AI, or less proximal to collection sites, were less likely to be recruited, with a mitigation_strategy of remote collection and recruitment designed to control more variables. representation_bias, five sites in the United States and Canada and fluent English speakers only, with a mitigation of Spanish-language expansion and remote collection. measurement_bias, cohorts screened by site and therefore collected on distinct iPad devices, varying headset microphone distance and diagnosis made by a single clinician or from EHR or prescription, with affected_subsets 'Disease cohort categories, which are confounded with collection site and device'. annotation_bias, a single label from a single labeler with diagnostic practice varying between sites and human-level performance varying widely across conditions. future_use_impacts carries the stereotyping and quality-of-service framing and the site/device signature warning. known_limitations adds five typed entries (coverage, representativeness, scope, temporal, coverage). anomalies records protocol change over the study and unaudited transcription models.
questions.quality_note: Strong systematic categorization: four distinct BiasTypeEnum values with substantive descriptions, mitigations on two, affected subsets on one, and the confounding structure between cohort, site and device identified explicitly, which is the most consequential bias in this dataset. Held to 4 because there is no fairness analysis in the quantitative sense the 5 anchor implies: no subgroup counts, no disparity measurement, no per-cohort or per-site performance consideration, and no explicit AI Ontology or CROISSANT RAI mapping. The bias claims are qualitative throughout, which is consistent with the record's complete absence of demographic figures noted under Q15.

strengths: Governance documented end to end across two access tiers: credentialed PhysioNet access with a signed Registered Access Agreement for the derived features, and a DACO-reviewed, institution-signed Data Transfer and Use Agreement route via Synapse for the raw audio, with license, IP terms, retention obligations, destruction certification and per-institution application scope all drawn from the same instruments.

Near-complete and unusually candid human-subjects coverage: USF single IRB with subsite approvals, four consent modes including a video-read statement that doubles as voice-identity verification, an explicit withdrawal mechanism with its post-collection limit, exact compensation amounts and caps, a nineteen-item Safe Harbor identifier list, and open statements that k-anonymity of two was not achieved and that a voice remains recognizable in principle.

Technical pipeline documented to reproduction-level specificity: monaural conversion and 16 kHz resampling with a Butterworth filter, then 25 ms windows at a 10 ms hop with a 400-point FFT, sixty MFCCs, articulatory traces at 50 Hz and forty-category posteriorgrams at 100 Hz, produced by eight named tools with b2aiprep 3.0.0 and repository URLs for the consortium libraries.

Collection instrumentation named at the level that matters for confounding: tablet generations, the Avid AE-36 microphone and its dongle, headset use, the REDCap capture path, and the resulting acknowledgement that cohorts are confounded with site and device.

Disciplined source handling throughout: five divergent grant identifier forms, participant-count and collection-target conflicts, the access-model change across releases, and healthsheet answers written against earlier versions and a different hosting platform are each declared with the resolution rule, and the companion pediatric dataset is kept out of this record's composition as a typed relation.
weaknesses: Not one demographic figure appears anywhere. The record names age, sex, gender, race, ethnicity, socioeconomic status and sexual orientation as recorded dimensions and states the dataset is skewed by disorder, site and demographics, but gives no per-cohort, per-site or per-attribute counts, so representativeness cannot be assessed quantitatively and the bias documentation stays qualitative.

Four generic keywords (health, biomarkers, bridge2ai, voice) against a description that enumerates modality, five cohorts, eight feature families, three formats and the access model, leaving discoverability far below the record's actual content.

No data protection impact assessment slot at all, despite a documented residual re-identification risk and a stated failure to reach k-anonymity of two, and the Data Access Compliance Office contact sits in maintainers rather than in regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact.

Two boolean-versus-content contradictions: content_warnings_present is false while the warnings list is populated, and confidential_elements_present is false while the record classifies the data restricted, records a Certificate of Confidentiality and quotes the DTUA describing the data as personally identifiable information under OMB M-07-16.

variables carries only four join keys against a dataset of dozens of phenotype and feature tables, parent_datasets and resources are empty, no byte size or file count is given, and version_access.latest_version_doi carries the concept DOI rather than the DOI of the latest version.
recommendations: Add per-cohort and per-site participant counts and the principal demographic distributions to subpopulations, and cross-reference them from known_biases so the representation and measurement bias claims carry figures.

Expand keywords to eight or more terms covering modality (speech, cough, acoustic features), cohort (voice disorders, neurological, psychiatric, respiratory), format (Parquet, TSV) and access model (credentialed access).

Populate data_protection_impacts with the analysis behind withholding the waveforms, or state that no assessment was conducted, and move DACO@b2ai-voice.org into regulatory_restrictions.governance_committee_contact.

Reconcile the two boolean contradictions: empty the content_warnings warnings list and relocate the superseded healthsheet warning to source_caveats, and state in confidential_elements which reading of the healthsheet question the false answer addresses.

Correct version_access.latest_version_doi to the version DOI 10.13026/8xbn-nq66, adopt one identifier form across related_datasets.target_dataset, and record total_file_count and total_size_bytes so the release size is stated rather than estimated from record counts.

Pin the tool versions for openSMILE, Praat, parselmouth, torchaudio, sparc, ppgs and senselab and identify the Whisper release rather than the model size, so the feature pipeline is reproducible as well as described.

Scope the quoted AI-readiness self-assessment in notes to the release and hosting platform it was written against, since the record's own evidence of PhysioNet hosting with version and concept DOIs contradicts its 'domain-appropriate criterion not met' finding.
